title: Tuning the fraud scorer
prompt: Your model scores every transaction for fraud in real time. Fraud that slips through is expensive to refund and reverse, but blocking a legitimate customer at checkout erodes trust and can lose them for good. How do you tune and architect the scoring decision?
constraint: Missed fraud is costly, but false positives that block real customers hurt trust just as much — you must protect recall without sacrificing the legitimate-customer experience.

options.why: Directly serves both halves of the constraint: confident transactions clear instantly (no trust damage), confident fraud is blocked, and the ambiguous middle band gets a deeper async/manual review instead of a blunt block-or-allow at checkout. You catch costly fraud without auto-rejecting borderline legitimate customers — best fit.

Defensible because missed fraud is explicitly costly, so leaning toward recall is reasonable. But maximizing recall alone drags in many false positives, blocking legitimate customers at checkout — which the constraint says hurts trust just as much. It addresses one side of the trade-off but neglects the other, so it's weaker than a tiered review.

Maximizing precision minimizes false positives but lets more real fraud through — exactly the costly misses the constraint warns against. It protects the customer experience while sacrificing recall, which the constraint refuses to trade away.

A single block-or-allow cutoff forces a lose-lose: set it low and you block many legitimate customers (trust damage); set it high and you miss costly fraud. It gives the borderline cases nowhere to go, violating both sides of the constraint at once.
